---
title: "Windows"
---

Windows preparation provides Git, uv, Python 3.12, and the stable release of Visual Studio Code. All Windows commands in this book use **PowerShell**. The optional SQL Server driver is needed only for Python connections to an actual SQL Server database.

## System and terminal

Windows Update in Settings provides the normal operating-system update route. Managed computers may require institutional software installation. Windows Developer Mode is not a prerequisite for these course tools.

PowerShell can be opened from the Start menu. In VS Code, Terminal: Select Default Profile selects PowerShell for new integrated terminals. Git Bash is a different shell; its path and environment-variable syntax should not be mixed with these commands.

## Git, uv, and Python

The [Git for Windows installer](https://git-scm.com/install/windows) supplies Git. Its setup should make Git available from the command line. After installation, a new PowerShell session can check the result:

```powershell
git --version
```

The [official uv installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) downloads and runs an installation script:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

The execution-policy option applies to that installer process. It is not a permanent change to the machine's execution policy. After a new terminal has loaded the updated PATH, these checks install and locate the course's Python version:

```powershell
uv --version
uv python install 3.12
uv python find 3.12
```

**Expected result:** Git and uv report versions, and the final command returns the path to a Python 3.12 executable. A separate global Python installation is unnecessary.

## Visual Studio Code

The stable [VS Code Windows installer](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/windows) provides the editor. The Microsoft Python extension (`ms-python.python`) adds Python editing and interpreter selection. File → Open Folder opens the course directory; Terminal → New Terminal opens PowerShell there.

The [project setup chapter](03-project-setup.qmd) creates the shared `.venv`. After that step, Python: Select Interpreter selects `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`. Project commands use `uv run`, so manual environment activation is unnecessary.

## Optional: SQL Server ODBC driver

The synthetic database exercise requires no server driver. Live Python connections use [Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/download-odbc-driver-for-sql-server?view=sql-server-ver17). The installer architecture must match Windows: x64 for Intel/AMD 64-bit systems, ARM64 for Windows on Arm, and x86 for 32-bit systems. Settings → System → About shows the system type. The Python process and driver must also have compatible architectures, especially when emulation is involved.

The installer presents its license terms. After installation, PowerShell can inspect driver registration:

```powershell
Get-OdbcDriver -Name "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server" |
    Select-Object Name, Platform
```

**Expected result:** a registered driver named `ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server` appears for the relevant platform. This confirms installation, not server access. Server addresses, permissions, and certificates are covered in [SQL Server connections](mssql-connection.qmd); editor queries are covered in [SQL Server in VS Code](mssql-vscode.qmd).

## Troubleshooting and exercise

If a command is unrecognised, a new terminal is the first check. `Get-Command git, uv` shows the executables PowerShell resolves. Missing results point to an installation or PATH problem. A driver listed only for a different platform suggests an architecture mismatch.

The setup exercise produces an environment report containing the PowerShell version (`$PSVersionTable.PSVersion`), Git and uv versions, the Python 3.12 path, and the course folder shown by `Get-Location`. No API keys or database passwords belong in the report.

**Success criteria:** the core tools are discoverable, VS Code opens the course root, and the SQL Server driver is either verified for a live exercise or explicitly recorded as unnecessary for offline work.
